headline: 34 workers killed in coal mine blast in southern Pakistan
summary: A suspected methane gas explosion tore through a mine in Balochistan, sparking a massive rescue operation to recover trapped miners.
details: At least 34 workers have been killed following a blast at a coal mine in southern Pakistan, according to the provincial disaster agency.
The explosion, suspected to be caused by methane gas, occurred on Thursday near the capital of the resource-rich province of Balochistan.
Rescue operations ran through the night, with teams recovering 34 bodies from the concrete tunnel by early Friday morning.
The tragedy was compounded when other miners rushed into the mine after the blast to attempt a rescue, only to be killed themselves.
The incident took place in Sorange, approximately 50 kilometres from the provincial capital, Quetta.
Mining accidents are frequent in Balochistan, leading to repeated calls from labour rights movements for stricter safety standards and enforcement.
While Balochistan is rich in coal, gold, and copper, it remains Pakistan's poorest province, lagging in education, employment, and economic development.
